description: ☰ → Terminal: a full-window view over the chat, as the Kubernetes view is, of tabs of Multiplex terminals, each run on a host by its host process (wire's terminal op) and drawn here. It can move out to a window of its own (Multiplex's look) and back.

parts.name: bar
parts.shows: The view's top bar: "Terminal" (heading), the shown terminal's host by name (dim), then flat buttons New tab and Move to Its Own Window, and a round Close (×).

actions.does: A new terminal on the host picked in the window's host dropdown, in a new tab

actions.by: click Move to Its Own Window
actions.does: The tabs move to a window titled Multiplex (its frame, a New tab button in its header); the view closes. Closing that window puts them back here, shown.
Closes the view; its terminals keep running and are there when it opens again

parts.name: tabs
parts.shows: A tab per terminal, titled by its program (else its host); the strip only with more than one tab, as Emission's and Multiplex's. A tab whose program ended while a Bot was at it says (ended) and stays till closed; any other closes as its program ends.

parts.name: terminal

decisions.said: Terminal keys as iTerm2 and Terminal.app have them: Cmd+T, Cmd+W, Cmd+C, Cmd+V on a Mac; Ctrl+Shift on Linux
decisions.rule: Every desktop app's terminal takes Cmd+T/W/C/V on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+T/W/C/V on Linux for new tab, close tab, copy and paste

decisions.said: Without VTE on macOS the error isn't clear; give proper guidance
decisions.rule: Every app without a terminal library says what to install, the command for its platform, and to restart

decisions.said: In Multiplex, Ctrl+L to clear the window adds to the scrollback: it seems to insert a lot of empty lines, which it shouldn't do at all
decisions.rule: Every terminal (Multiplex's tabs, the Terminal view, a Kubernetes pod's shell, on any app and any viewer of a host's terminal) clears its screen (Ctrl+L, clear) as iTerm2 does: the rows down to the lowest one written go into the scrollback with no blank screen of rows after them, so clearing again and again adds only the prompt's row each time. The terminal library keeps its own spawning, typing, paste and resizing; the clear is rewritten in the bytes the program writes, before any viewer gets them. On the alternate screen or with a scroll region set, a clear is left as it is

decisions.said: Icons don't really work in Multiplex: the Nerd Font icons ls and fish print show as boxes (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's terminal draws Nerd Font icons (their private-use code points) from Symbols Nerd Font Mono wherever its own font has none: the app bundles that font (an installed one is used too), so the icons draw on macOS and Linux with nothing installed

parts.shows: The terminal (VTE), its edges glowing in the accent while a Bot is at its terminal tools there. What's typed goes to the program on its host. A host that can't be reached says why in it. Cmd+C and Cmd+V copy and paste, Cmd+T and Cmd+W open and close a tab (Ctrl+Shift with the same letters on Linux). Nerd Font icons (ls, prompts) draw from Symbols Nerd Font Mono where its font has none. Ctrl+L (or clear) clears the screen, keeping the rows written in the scrollback and no blank rows after them. Without VTE (see states: VTE missing).

states.name: VTE missing
states.shows: VTE's GTK 4 build isn't in the app: ☰ → Terminal opens the view with the missing-dependency state in place of its tabs: a package icon, "Terminal needs VTE", this platform's install command with Copy (copying toasts "Copied: run it in a terminal, then Restart"), and Restart (the app's own library is loaded as it starts). Its new-tab and out-to-a-window buttons are greyed. Multiplex, started without it, says the same in a line on stderr.

decisions.said: Without VTE on macOS the error isn't clear; give proper guidance, and fold it into the general dependency guidance (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app without a terminal library shows the missing-dependency state where the terminal would be (☰ → Terminal, a Kubernetes pod's shell), with the platform's install command and Restart; never only a toast
